new_closed_values.name: WAF_CHALLENGE
new_closed_values.set: capture failure reason (record.reason, matched by host_capture._REASON and forwarded as CAPTURE_FAILED:<failure_class>:<reason>), under the EXISTING failure class UNEXPECTED_CHALLENGE; also a new classifyResponse state of the same name

four_postulates.i_mece: Domain: why a capture failure carries a reason. The ChallengeFailure reasons so far name a SCREEN (CHALLENGE_ONE_TIME_CODE_UNSUPPORTED, _CAPTCHA_, _WAF_INTERSTITIAL, _FORCED_PASSWORD_RESET, _UNRECOGNISED_SCREEN, _ATTENDED_TIMEOUT); the AuthError reasons name where a sign-in stopped. A probe reply that is a challenge after an accepted sign-in is in neither: it is not a screen (the identity page loaded and passed) and not a rejected sign-in. By subtraction from the printed census (9 AuthError reasons, 6 screen reasons) it is the uncovered member; no existing value covers it.
four_postulates.ii_same_grain: Same grain as its siblings: one closed upper-case token per failure site, set on record.reason and passing _REASON.
four_postulates.iii_one_intent: It means exactly one thing: the probe reply (not the screen) met the READ path's challenge test. The name is the READ path's own (controller.py classify_pull reason WAF_CHALLENGE).
four_postulates.iv_state_coherence: Remedy differs from its neighbours: CHALLENGE_WAF_INTERSTITIAL moves with a different screen or an attended hold; SIGNIN_FORM_REPRESENTED and NO_AUTHENTICATED_PROBE move with the credential or the account; WAF_CHALLENGE moves with the WAF token / client class (the pair, now sent only with a token) and does not move the credential, the account lock state or the sign-in count. It does NOT change failure_class values (UNEXPECTED_CHALLENGE is reused), the 9 AuthError sites (test_host_capture asserts 9) or the READ path's pull reason of the same spelling, which is a different field in a different process (broker.py:386 compares pull['reason'], never a capture reason).

pair_rule_in_words: The with-token/without-token probe pair is sent only when the cookie jar holds an aws-waf-token. With none, both arms would send the same request, so the pair is not sent, the receipt's probe_pair carries discriminating=false with only the without_token members of the one request that was sent, and one stderr line says so; with a token the pair runs as before and carries discriminating=true.
